([[Austin, Texas]]) | college = [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] (2020–2021) | highlights = * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Newcomer Team (2021) * Big 12 All-Freshman Team (2021) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2020]]) * [[Texas Mr. Basketball]] (2020) * Texas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] }} '''Gregory James Brown III''' (born September 1, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. ==Early life and high school career== Brown grew up playing basketball under the guidance of his uncle, [[Roderick Anderson]], a former professional basketball player.{{cite web |last1=Clynch |first1=Shawn |title=A U.T. basketball great mentoring a rising star |url=https://www.kvue.com/article/sports/a-ut-basketball-great-mentoring-a-rising-star/301100881 |website=[[KVUE]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=August 17, 2016}} Brown attended [[Vandegrift High School]] in [[Austin, Texas]], where he was a four-year [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball starter, in addition to competed in varsity [[track and field]] in the [[high jump]]. As a freshman, he recorded his first [[double (basketball)|triple-double]] with 15 points, 14 rebounds and a school-record 18 blocks in a win over [[Hutto High School]].{{cite web |last1=Riggs |first1=Randy |title=Vandegrift freshman Brown III soaring to statistical heights |url=https://www.statesman.com/NEWS/20170111/Vandegrift-freshman-Brown-III-soaring-to-statistical-heights |website=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=January 11, 2017}} In his freshman season, Brown averaged 17.2 points, 10.7 rebounds and 3.6 blocks per game, earning All-Central Texas Newcomer of the Year honors from the ''[[Austin American-Statesman]]''.{{cite web |last1=Field |first1=Carson |title=Brown looks to shine in second season at Vandegrift |url=https://www.fourpointsnews.com/2017/10/20/brown-looks-shine-second-season-vandegrift/ |publisher=Four Points News |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=October 20, 2017}} As a sophomore, Brown averaged 27.4 points, 12.3 rebounds, and 2.5 blocks per game en route to District 25-6A offensive [[most valuable player]] (MVP) accolades. He led the district in scoring and rebounding.{{cite web |last1=Wells |first1=Justin |title=One-on-One with 5-star Greg Brown III |url=https://insidetexas.com/one-on-one-with-5-star-greg-brown-iii/ |publisher=Inside Texas |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=March 15, 2018}} In his junior season, Brown averaged 30.1 points, 13.5 rebounds and 5.4 blocks per game. He missed 14 games early in the season with a dislocated finger. Brown was named to the All-Central Texas first team for his third straight year.{{cite web |last1=Bils |first1=Chris |title='Highlight reel' Greg Brown III happy to carry a heavy load for Vandegrift |url=https://www.statesman.com/sports/20190328/highlight-reel-greg-brown-iii-happy-to-carry-heavy-load-for-vandegrift |website=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=March 28, 2019}} As a senior, he averaged 26.1 points, 13.2 rebounds and 3.5 blocks per game, collecting District 13-6A MVP, Texas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and ''Austin American-Statesman'' All-Central Texas Player of the Year honors. Brown led Vandegrift to a program-best 33–3 record and its first district title. He was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], which was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=March 30, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Thomas |title=Greg Brown III leads honors in District 13-6A boys basketball |url=https://www.alicetx.com/sports/20200330/greg-brown-iii-leads-honors-in-district-13-6a-boys-basketball |website=[[Alice Echo-News Journal]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=March 30, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Hamilton |first1=Brian |title=Greg Brown could remain Austin’s hometown hero, but the top recruit has options |url=https://theathletic.com/1738044/2020/04/13/greg-brown-could-remain-austins-hometown-hero-but-the-top-recruit-has-options/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=April 13, 2020}}{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Thomas |title=All-Central Texas boys basketball team: Vandegrift star Greg Brown III adds to honors |url=https://www.statesman.com/sports/20200409/all-central-texas-boys-basketball-team-vandegrift-star-greg-brown-iii-adds-to-honors |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=April 9, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== Brown drew the attention of major [[college basketball]] programs before high school. In his freshman year, he emerged as one of the best players in the 2020 class and held basketball offers from several schools, including [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]]. By the end of his high school career, Brown was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and a top-10 player in the 2020 class, according to major recruiting services. He trimmed his offers to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] or Texas, or opt to instead play professionally.{{cite web |last1=Howe |first1=Jeff |title=Going pro an option for five-star Texas target Greg Brown |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas/Article/Greg-Brown-III-college-basketball-recruiting-G-League-option-April-24-decision-Texas-Longhorns-146146085/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=April 22, 2020 |date=April 16, 2020}} On April 24, 2020, he announced his commitment to Texas over Auburn, Memphis, Michigan, Kentucky and a $300,000 offer from the G League.{{cite news a freshman, Brown averaged 9.3 points and 6.2 rebounds per game.
